master.description:
an assignment master overlaid on the tool folders' quantities.toml (beside this file)

overlays the tool folders' mappings key by key (`[quantities.<tool>.compatible_quantities]`): an entry for a (tool, quantity) pair replaces the framework's. The file must exist.

import.description:
errand files whose tables this one starts from, in order; this file wins (V56, V93, V94)

errand files this one starts from, in order, named as `heimdall run` names a config: `name` is a file beside this one (`name.toml`), `<A>/<E>` another assignment's, `./…` from the work dir; `.toml` optional. **This file wins** (V56): a quantity, tool table or configuration of the file replaces the imported one whole; `[plot]`, `[static]`, `[prelim]` and `[errand]`'s own keys merge key by key, tables recursively. Imports nest (V94): an imported file's own imports come first, depth-first; a circle is refused. Another assignment's file keeps its bare paths (cards, filters, styles, executables) its own assignment's, so its tools plan as they do in it. The file that imports sets its own `[errand].name` and `assignment`; no folder of its configurations may be an imported errand's (V100). An entry may be `{ from = "<config>", only = ["quantities", "cfgs.default", …] }`: only those sections or dotted keys of that file, each of which it must have (V95). `--show-config` says where each quantity, tool and configuration came from.

drop.description:
dotted keys taken out of what the imports gave, before this file's tables (V95)

dotted keys (`cfgs.default4`, `plot.figures.statistics`, `quantities.radius`, `tools.jets`) taken out of what the imports brought in, before this file's own tables are laid over them (V95). Each must name something an import gave, so a misspelt drop is refused rather than keeping what it meant to remove; a file that imports nothing has nothing to drop.

vars.description:
names said once and cited anywhere in the file as {var:name} (V96)

`name = value`, cited in any string of the file as `{var:name}` and replaced when the file is read, after its imports and `--set`, so an identity sees only the result (V96). A string that is exactly one var takes its value as it is: `event_count = "{var:events}"` is an integer, and a list stays a list; inside a longer string a var must be a scalar (`"rivet:{var:ana}"`). An unknown name is refused with the nearest. An imported file's `{var:…}` takes this file's value, so a shared file can be written with parameters; its own `[config.vars]` come with whatever is taken of it (`only` included, V101), under this file's. Imports are read before vars, so an import's name cannot cite one; `--set config.vars.<name>=…` changes one for a job.

meta.description:
about the file, for people; versions: the stack it was run with, warned about, never enforced (V97)

descriptive: it never changes a point (V97). Any key is free text for people (`author`, `references`, …) except `versions = { pythia8 = "8.317", rivet = "4.1.3" }`: the packages of `env/stack.toml` the file was run with, each version a string. A version the stack does not have (`6.5` matches 6.5.6) is a **warning** in `--plan`, at the job's start and in `heimdall check`, which still passes: the job goes ahead, at your own risk. A package stack.toml does not name is refused, since its warning could never come.

the configuration heimdall run runs (required unless sweep_runs)

the NN_ before each Run's folder name

tag.description:
the tag each Run is given when it runs, unless it has one (a letter or digit, then letters, digits, . _ + -; at most 40)

default for configurations: a short name kept with the Run (its record's `tag` file and its plot document's `[source].tag`), which `heimdall runs`, `heimdall status` and a report show beside it. FIFOs made in the point's folder before the tools start

named pipes in the point's output directory. A FIFO connects tools **in one group** only, has **one reader**, and never feeds a tool that is not `streamable` (C6).

regular files in the point's output directory, **kept**: the way to keep events for another configuration

a tool folder: shipped, the machine's or the work dir's (heimdall tools)

a tool folder's name (05 §3): Heimdall's `framework/tools/`, the machine root's or the work dir's `tools/` (`heimdall tools` lists them); `"exec"` runs any executable, `"module"` a `Module.hh` program

baseconfig.description:
base card(s), beside the file naming them

native base card(s), read in order (a bare name beside the file naming it). Tools with a card only.

what it reads: an interface or a file

what it reads: `[prelim]` names, another tool's `output_file`, a pre product, (post) a product of every point, or a path. The first input is `{input}`.

what it writes: an interface or a product

what it writes. An array is fan-out: App_Pythia writes the same events to each (V16). Exactly one writer per output (C6).

the tool fails when it runs longer

seconds of silence before it counts as stalled (default 300)

the tool fails when silent this long: no log line, status message or heartbeat (a prepare step waits at least 3600)

`"standard"` (`$HEIMDALL_STATUS_FD`), `"filters"` (the folder's `filters.toml`), `"none"`

a filters.toml of your own (beside the file naming it), in place of its folder's

your own rules in place of the folder's, a bare name beside the file naming it; implies `status = "filters"` (V61)

is its event count checked against the producer's sidecar?

native card settings, as written: "HeavyIon:mode" = 1 (over the base card, under quantities)

native card settings as written, `"HeavyIon:mode" = 1`, with no base card needed: over the base card, refused when a quantity sets the same key (one source per key, C8); a tool with no card refuses them (V59)

cores.description:
cores it keeps busy, for --plan's note (default: estimated)

how many cores it keeps busy, for `--plan`'s note and the crowded warning (V60); an integrated program is estimated as the generator's threads and one more

shards.description:
K processes on a share of the events each

K > 1: K processes of this tool, each on a share of the events, merged into its `output_file` by the folder's merge tool (V31; rivet, 05 §5.1). The chain is unchanged.

equivalent.description: the inputs are replicas of one process (-e): averaged σ

analyses.description: the analyses to run, with options: "photo_eic:R=0.4"

select.description: YODA path globs to convert (default: everything but /RAW, /TMP)

values.description:
the values

scalars or arrays (an energy pair)

tags.description:
one per value: folder and point names

one per value. The default is the value with anything but `A–Za–z0–9.+-` replaced by `-`. Tags name point directories: keep them short and unique.

labels.description:
one per value: legend text

legend text, in **LaTeX** (`$e^-$`, `$\sqrt{s}$`), the one label language of every text an errand file gives a page (V65): math in `$…$`, the rest text, where a bare `_` or `^` is the character (`"PDF4LHC21_40"`). A label written in ROOT's TLatex (`#sqrt{s}`, `p_{T}` with no `$`) is refused, with its LaTeX as the hint; `heimdall migrate` rewrites it (V79). `\_`, `\^` and `\#` also give the character, even before a brace; in TOML write them in single quotes, `'PDF4LHC21\_40'`, since in `"…"` a backslash starts a TOML escape

shape.description:
a user quantity's value shape, as the vocabulary's: "pdg", "float|int", ["float", "float"] (V76)

the values' shape, in the vocabulary's grammar (V76): `"pdg"`, `"float|int"`, `["float", "float"]`; checked when the TOML is read. For a quantity of your own (one the vocabulary, `framework/schema/quantities.toml`, does not name); a vocabulary quantity has its own shape

styles.description:
one per value: its curves' look, { colour, line, width } (V67)

one per value (V67): its curves' look, `{ colour, line, width }`. `colour` is `"#rrggbb"`, a ROOT name (`"kBlue+1"`) or number (the yoda backend draws `#rrggbb` only); `line` is `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted` or `dashdot`; `width` is in points. A key left out, or `"default"`, is the style's; curves with no colour take the palette in turn, as mkhtml's take its cycle. A value keeps its look on every page, so a PDF is one colour throughout. With two curve axes, the later one's keys win

key.description:
the native key, or { <tool or tag> = key }

the native key. A string needs a `target`. A table entry for a tool tag wins over one for its type.

format.description:
how the value is written: a Python format, "{}*GeV"

a Python format for the value: `"{}*GeV"`

exclude.description:
1-based value places a sweep leaves out

values a sweep leaves out, by their **1-based** place (as `static = "#2"` and `--points 2` count): `exclude = [2]` sweeps the others. The remaining points keep their names and identities and are numbered 1… over what is swept. In an entangled group, a value any member excludes leaves the group. `static` may still pick an excluded value. Refused: a place outside 1…len(values), or none left (V42)

backend.description:
root (Paint), yoda (deprecated, rivet-mkhtml), mpl (matplotlib, V71), a list of them, or both (root and yoda)

`"root"` (Paint), `"yoda"` (deprecated, rivet-mkhtml; frozen, V71), `"mpl"` (matplotlib, mkhtml's pages drawn in-process: V71), `"both"` (root and yoda, V28) or an array of them, from the same pages

formats.description:
the pages' formats

`pdf`, `png`, `svg`, `eps`. mkhtml writes pdf and png always. The root backend writes `plots/<set>/root/index.html` (V70, V164): a section per cell, each page by its PNG or SVG, else an embedded PDF, linked to every format; add `png` for thumbnails a browser shows at once

band.description:
curve-axis quantities drawn as one curve, their first value, with the min–max envelope of all their values (V69)

curve axes drawn as an envelope (V69): per value of the other curve axes, one curve, the band quantity's first value, with the min–max of all its values shaded around it in the curve's colour (the usual PDF or scale band). Its legend entry ends `(<q> envelope)`; its own statistical errors are not drawn. A name that is not a curve axis of the configuration (swept, not `plot_points`, not combined) is refused at plan time. The yoda backend draws the same envelope as mkhtml's error band

objects.description:
YODA path globs that get pages (default: every 1D object)

matched against the option-free YODA path (`/photo_eic/d01-x01-y01`) or any variant's path. No object matching is an error.

ratio.description:
a ratio pad

a ratio pad: each curve over the data, or over the first curve when there are no data

y_gutter.description:
the top of the y axis at (1 + g) × the largest value

the top of the y axis at (1 + g) × the largest drawn value (on a log axis, g of the decades shown); `0`: no headroom. `"native"`: no gutter, the tool's own range (V29, V55; a v2 file's [plot] says `"default"`)

x_gutter.description:
x widened by g of its span

widens x by g of its span, symmetrically (in decades on a log axis). `"default"`: the range the bins give

x_range.description:
the x axis limits

the x axis limits, `[minimum, maximum]`, each end a number or `"default"`: the layer below's end (a figure's `["default", 10]` keeps `[plot]`'s minimum), and in `[plot]` the range the page calculates. They only show: the statistics are taken over the calculated range. A heat map and a statistic figure take them from their own figure alone; a heat map's are kept within its histogram and widened to whole bins, and a range that misses the histogram is refused

y_range.description:
the y axis limits

the y axis limits, `[minimum, maximum]`, each end as in `x_range`. It only cuts what is drawn: the statistics and the ratios are the curves' own values, and the ratio pad cuts at its own range. A numeric end holds when a curve passes it: Paint and mpl clip the curve, and a point's bar or a band reaching in, at the frame, and mark each bin past it with a thin line in the curve's colour, 2 px outside the frame (inside where a joined ratio pad leaves no room); curves past it in one bin share its width. The data are never marked, nor a value <= 0 on a log axis

logz.description:
a heat map's log z (default: the .plot's LogZ, V87)

a heat map's colour scale (V87)

auto_range.description:
x clipped to the bins with content

trim x to the bins with content, in curves and data

normalise.description:
"area": every curve and the data scaled to unit area over the bins drawn (V68)

`"area"` (V68): every curve, and the data, scaled to unit area, Σ value × bin width over the bins drawn (after voiding and the data's alignment), so pages compare shapes. Both backends scale the same way. The y label stays the `.plot`'s: set `y_label` (e.g. `"$1/\sigma\,\mathrm{d}\sigma/\mathrm{d}E_T$"`) on the pages it applies to. A figure (04 §11.2) may set it for its own

void_empty.description:
blank the bins empty in every curve

blank a bin that is zero in **every** curve

use_data.description:
false: [plot.data] stays but is not drawn

`false`: the `[plot.data]` table stays in the file but is not drawn, and a `ratio` divides each curve by the page's first curve, the first value of its curve axis (V44)

min_entries.description:
blank the bins with fewer raw entries

blank a bin that fewer raw entries went into, in **any** curve (read from the `/RAW` twin; objects without one are not voided this way)

range_pad.description:
whole bins added around auto_range

whole bins kept either side of the filled ones

sets.description:
page folders of chosen points: [[1, 4], "py8", "all"] (V159), or tables of page axes and curve groups, { name, pages = { … }, curves = [{ … }] } (V163)

the pages' cells, instead of the `plot_points` grid. An entry is a selector, a list of them (`set<k>`, its place), or a table. A selector (V159) is a 1-based index (as `point i/n` counts), a point's name, a glob of names (`"sh3_NNPDF40*"`), a tag of a quantity's (`"py8"`: every point with it), `"quantity=tag"`, or `"all"`; a string entry names its folder (`"pdf=X"` → `pdf-X`); its points are its curves, in the order named. A table (V163, `[[plot.sets]]`): `name` (its folder, default `set<k>`), `points` (selectors), `pages` (a filter whose quantities are the page axes: a cell per combination of their values among the set's points, `<set>/<cell>/<object>`), `curves` (a filter, or a list of them: the union, in order), `reference` (a filter: the curve moved first on each page), `look` (`{ colour = "<q>", line = "<q>" }`, or `"palette"`; with none, two varying curve axes: the one of at most 4 values the line), and any page key of `[plot]`, `objects` and `style` for its pages. A filter is `{ quantity = "all" | tag | glob | "!tag" | number | [those] }`: every combination of its quantities' values (an outer product). In `curves`, a value may carry its curves' look: `{ tag = "…", colour, line, width }`, or several values' in order, `{ tags = "all" | […] (or all = true), colours = […], lines = […], widths = […] }` (`color`, `colors` accepted). A swept quantity a table names in neither pages nor curves, taking several values, pages too, and the stage says so. A selector, tag or quantity no point has is refused at plan time. merged, scan and compare figures page by `plot_points` only

looks.description:
each value's look on every page, by quantity and tag: [plot.looks.pdf] NNPDF23lo = "#0067A5" (or { colour, line, width }) (V171)

[plot.looks.<quantity>] (V171): a value's look on every page and in every Run, by its tag: a colour (`"#rrggbb"`, a ROOT name or number) or `{ colour, line, width }`. A tag a Run does not have is unused, so a value commented out keeps its look. Over the quantity's own styles; a set's look, and a curves filter's styled values, over it; a set's automatic look leaves an axis with looks alone

across.description:

class.description:
how its pages are built: defined (an analysis object's own), overlay (several objects of each point), merged (the objects' pages with the points merged over `over`), compare (the objects' pages across configurations), derived (a new object from the objects, per point), scan (one number per point against a swept quantity), sheet (drawn pages in a grid)

how the pages are built. `defined`: an analysis object's own pages, `<cell>/<object>`, its curves the cell's points (and option variants). `overlay`: several objects of each point on one page, `<cell>/<name>`; a curve per object and point, labelled by `labels` (plus the point's, when the page has several); a ratio divides by the first curve. `merged` (V82): the objects' pages, `<cell>/<name>/<object>`, with the points merged over the `over` axes: per value of the other axes, their YODAs merged by the combine folder's command (`rivet-merge -e`: statistics add, σ averaged), once per change of a member's YODA, into `.cache/…/merged/<name>/`. The run keeps its points apart; the figure alone merges them (`combine` merges them for the whole configuration). `sheet` (V89): drawn pages laid out in a grid (`pages`, `columns`; below). `compare` (V83): the objects' pages across configurations, `<E>/compare/<name>/<cell>/<object>` beside the configurations' own folders (in `records/` and `results/`, a folder per backend). A curve per configuration and point (or combined group), labelled by the configuration (`labels`, else its `label`) and then the point's curve axes. The configurations must have the same page and curve axes (checked at plan time); the figure is drawn by the plot stage of each of them once all have complete points, and says what it waits for otherwise (`heimdall plot` draws it too). `derived` (V84): a new object per point, `/FIGURES/<name>` (`/FIGURES:R=0.4/<name>` per analysis-option variant): `op = "ratio"`, `"difference"` or `"sum"` of its two objects (histograms made estimates first; the same binning, else an error naming both), or `"projection-x"`/`"projection-y"` of its one 2D object (summed over the other axis: a histogram's weights, an estimate's values × widths, as a Scatter2D whose x ranges are the bins). It is appended to a copy of each point's YODA (`.cache/…/derived/`, remade when the product or the figures change, by `framework/plot/figures/derive.py`: YODA's Python, so `gjallarhorn`), and is then an object like any: its pages `<cell>/<name>` (labels from its first object's `.plot`; set `y_label`), an overlay or a merged or compare figure may name it (`"r15"`). `scan` (V85): one number per point against a swept quantity: `x` a curve axis whose values are numbers, `y` = `sigma` (the point's `/_XSEC`), `entries` (its events, or its object's raw entries), or `integral`, `mean`, `bin:N` of its one object. A page per cell, `<cell>/<name>`, a curve per value of the other curve axes: a Scatter2D, a point per x value with an x range halfway to its neighbours centred on it (so every backend can draw it as a bin; it is drawn as markers, `type = "Scatter2D"`). Axis titles: the quantity's name and the y read, until set. A quantity of names (PDF sets) cannot be an x yet

The page TOML says `markers = true`; mkhtml and mpl draw the curves as they draw points (`ConnectBins=0`, with their x bars). `HeatMap` (V87): a 2D object (a YODA `Histo2D` or `Estimate2D`), the default for one: a page per point of the cell, `<cell>/<object>/<point>`, coloured by value with its scale on the right (labels from the `.plot`, `ZLabel` and `LogZ` too; no ratio, data or voiding). class.description:
how its pages are built: defined (an analysis object's own), overlay (several objects of each point), merged (the objects' pages with the points merged over `over`), compare (the objects' pages across configurations), derived (a new object from the objects, per point), scan (one number per point against a swept quantity), sheet (drawn pages in a grid)

how the pages are built. `defined`: an analysis object's own pages, `<cell>/<object>`, its curves the cell's points (and option variants). `overlay`: several objects of each point on one page, `<cell>/<name>`; a curve per object and point, labelled by `labels` (plus the point's, when the page has several); a ratio divides by the first curve. `merged` (V82): the objects' pages, `<cell>/<name>/<object>`, with the points merged over the `over` axes: per value of the other axes, their YODAs merged by the combine folder's command (`rivet-merge -e`: statistics add, σ averaged), once per change of a member's YODA, into `.cache/…/merged/<name>/`. The run keeps its points apart; the figure alone merges them (`combine` merges them for the whole configuration). `sheet` (V89): drawn pages laid out in a grid (`pages`, `columns`; below). `compare` (V83): the objects' pages across configurations, `<E>/compare/<name>/<cell>/<object>` beside the configurations' own folders (in `records/` and `results/`, a folder per backend). A curve per configuration and point (or combined group), labelled by the configuration (`labels`, else its `label`) and then the point's curve axes. The configurations must have the same page and curve axes (checked at plan time); the figure is drawn by the plot stage of each of them once all have complete points, and says what it waits for otherwise (`heimdall plot` draws it too). `derived` (V84): a new object per point, `/FIGURES/<name>` (`/FIGURES:R=0.4/<name>` per analysis-option variant): `op = "ratio"`, `"difference"` or `"sum"` of its two objects (histograms made estimates first; the same binning, else an error naming both), or `"projection-x"`/`"projection-y"` of its one 2D object (summed over the other axis: a histogram's weights, an estimate's values × widths, as a Scatter2D whose x ranges are the bins). It is appended to a copy of each point's YODA (`.cache/…/derived/`, remade when the product or the figures change, by `framework/plot/figures/derive.py`: YODA's Python, so `gjallarhorn`), and is then an object like any: its pages `<cell>/<name>` (labels from its first object's `.plot`; set `y_label`), an overlay or a merged or compare figure may name it (`"r15"`). `scan` (V85): one number per point against a swept quantity: `x` a curve axis whose values are numbers, `y` = `sigma` (the point's `/_XSEC`), `entries` (its events, or its object's raw entries), or `integral`, `mean`, `bin:N` of its one object. A page per cell, `<cell>/<name>`, a curve per value of the other curve axes: a Scatter2D, a point per x value with an x range halfway to its neighbours centred on it (so every backend can draw it as a bin; it is drawn as markers, `type = "Scatter2D"`). Axis titles: the quantity's name and the y read, until set. A quantity of names (PDF sets) cannot be an x yet

what is drawn: Hist1D (steps), Scatter2D (a marker per bin, as data: V86), HeatMap (a 2D object coloured, a page per point: V87); default: from the objects (2D: HeatMap), a scan's Scatter2D

what is drawn: `Hist1D`, steps per curve; `Scatter2D` (V86), a marker per bin at its centre with its y error, in the curve's colour (`data.marker`, `data.marker_size` of the style), as Paint draws data; the legend shows the marker. The page TOML says `markers = true`; mkhtml and mpl draw the curves as they draw points (`ConnectBins=0`, with their x bars). `HeatMap` (V87): a 2D object (a YODA `Histo2D` or `Estimate2D`), the default for one: a page per point of the cell, `<cell>/<object>/<point>`, coloured by value with its scale on the right (labels from the `.plot`, `ZLabel` and `LogZ` too; no ratio, data or voiding). max_running.description:
at most this many points at once (the array's %K); 0: no limit

the points array's throttle, `--array=1-N%K`; `0`: as many as the scheduler gives. `parallelism` is not used: each job is one point

mail.description:
mail this address when a job ends or fails

`sbatch --mail-user`, with `--mail-type=END,FAIL`

setup.description:
shell lines each job runs before Heimdall's gjallarhorn.sh (module loads)

shell lines each job runs first, before it sources Heimdall's `gjallarhorn.sh` (`"module load gcc/13"`): what the nodes need that the login shell had

image.description:
run each job in this Apptainer image: a name of <machine root>/images, or a .sif's path

the image's own Heimdall and stack run the job (`apptainer exec --cleanenv`, or `singularity`), with the work dir bound at its own path; `setup` still runs first, on the node (`"module load apptainer"`). `heimdall image build` makes one (V150)

sbatch.description:
any other sbatch options, as written

any other `sbatch` options, each as written (`"--exclusive"`, `"--export=NONE"`, `"--reservation=r"`), after the ones the keys above give

pre.description:
time, memory, cpus, … for the pre job only

the resource keys (`time`, `partition`, `account`, `qos`, `constraint`, `gres`, `memory`, `cpus`, `sbatch`) for the pre job only, over the others

finish.description:
time, memory, cpus, … for the finish job only (combine, post, plots)

the resource keys for the finish job only (the combined groups, the post tools and the plots), over the others; its `cpus` default to 1
